key_insight: The paper argues that control theory, optimal transport, probabilistic inference, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and machine learning are unified by optimizing free-energy-like objectives under dynamical or statistical constraints.
engineering_relevance: This perspective helps engineers transfer algorithms and intuitions across reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling when designing scalable learning systems.
method: Build a conceptual bridge across five fields using a common variational/free-energy framework.
Review core principles from physics first, then map them to learning applications.
Highlight selected use cases in reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling.
evidence_signal: As a review paper, it synthesizes theory and applications rather than presenting new experimental data or benchmark evaluation in the abstract.
watch_item: Because the work is a conceptual review, practical adoption may require translating the unified theory into problem-specific assumptions, solvers, and numerical approximations.
paper_title: Bridging Control, Inference, Transport, and Thermodynamics: From Theory to Applications in Learning
